items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One I knew before was Roger Paraboschi... Jaques Hess played guitar, Maxime Saury, clarinet... The style of the band was a mixture of New Orleans and swing.

ctx.x: But what surprised me most of all was that these fellows were all young and not one was over 30 and they knew most of all the jazz standards and classics' that I knew and some modern ones that I didn't know. So there was no sweat getting a programme together. But I could not remember the musicians' names, so when we were doing the concert to a full house, I presented the pianist as Barney, the saxophonist as Mike, the vibraphone player was Joe, the bass player John, and the drummer - Rodger. Another surprise was…

And I was also surprised at the large following that jazz had as compared to the public that afternoon in the theatre. I suppose I was better known to the jazz public here than I realized I was, because I had never had such a warm and enthusiastic reception. I was happy about the way the musicians had supported me, and after the concert, my old friend Maurice Cullaz and his wife Yvonette, whom I had known very well since 1935, came backstage to greet me. I was surprised to see the wife of Frans Jackson whose name…

When all the greetings were over, Charles taken me to the hotel where a room had been reserved in the neighbourhood of Montmartre which I was familiar with. He left me and I was on my own. The hotel was called "la Bruyère" and was situated on the corner of a street by the same name and rue Pigalle, not far from the Hotel Eden where I had stayed when I came to Paris in 1935. After unpacking my bags, I decided to go out especially to Boudon's and the tabac at the corner of rue Fontaine to see if I could find any…
